plan: [ It's a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value: I win exactly when my value exceeds all others and pay the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit and avoiding losses from overbidding. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins. There’s no useful history (1 round). Avoid any epsilon “tie-break” above value; that can force winning at a price above value. Therefore, bid exactly my value of 26.0. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies, since if you win you pay the second-highest bid (≤ your bid), and shading risks losing profitable wins while overbidding risks negative payoff. With no informative history and 3 bidders, stick to truthful bidding. My value is 31, so I bid 31.0 (increments of 0.1 allowed). Ties are random; truthful bidding remains optimal. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy. With no history to exploit and only 1 round, maximizing expected profit means bidding my exact value. My value is $24, so I bid 24 to win whenever opponents’ top value is below 24 and pay the second-highest bid, ensuring nonnegative profit if I win. ]
